# Overview

This vignette starts from a Seurat object in which the analysis is already done, adds the tables that CerebroNexus pre-computes (most expressed genes, marker genes, enriched pathways), and exports everything to a `.crb` file.
It does not cover quality control, normalization, clustering or dimensional reduction; for those steps, please see the [Seurat tutorials](https://satijalab.org/seurat/).

The functions shown here take a Seurat object.
The same steps, except the gene set enrichment, can also be switched on in the Builder (`launchCerebroBuilder()`); see [Build a data set by pointing](https://www.mheming.com/CerebroNexus/articles/build_a_data_set_by_pointing.html).
If your analysis lives in a SingleCellExperiment or an AnnData (scanpy) file, see [Show your Seurat, scanpy and SingleCellExperiment analysis with CerebroNexus](https://www.mheming.com/CerebroNexus/articles/import_your_analysis.html).

# Installation

Install `CerebroNexus` and [`Seurat`](https://satijalab.org/seurat/).
[`GSVA`](https://bioconductor.org/packages/release/bioc/html/GSVA.html) and [`qvalue`](https://bioconductor.org/packages/release/bioc/html/qvalue.html) are only needed for the gene set enrichment step.

```{r installation, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, eval=FALSE}
if ( 'BiocManager' %in% installed.packages() == FALSE ) install.packages('BiocManager')
if ( 'remotes' %in% installed.packages() == FALSE ) install.packages('remotes')

library(BiocManager)

if ( !'CerebroNexus' %in% rownames(installed.packages()) ) remotes::install_github('mihem/CerebroNexus')
if ( 'Seurat' %in% installed.packages() == FALSE ) install('Seurat')
if ( 'GSVA' %in% installed.packages() == FALSE ) install('GSVA')
if ( 'qvalue' %in% installed.packages() == FALSE ) install('qvalue')
```

# Start from a processed Seurat object

CerebroNexus expects an object in which the usual analysis is done:

* normalized expression values,
* at least one grouping variable in the meta data, e.g. samples or clusters,
* at least one dimensional reduction, e.g. UMAP or t-SNE.

Here we use `pbmc_small`, a processed example of 80 cells and 230 genes that ships with Seurat.
It carries clusters, an arbitrary two-level grouping (`groups`), and PCA and t-SNE coordinates.
We copy the clusters to `seurat_clusters`, the column name Seurat uses in a standard analysis.
With your own data, load your object instead and use your own column names.

```{r setup, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, eval=FALSE}
library(Seurat)
library(CerebroNexus)

set.seed(1234567)

data('pbmc_small')
seurat <- UpdateSeuratObject(pbmc_small)
seurat$seurat_clusters <- seurat$RNA_snn_res.1
```

# CerebroNexus functions

Now we use CerebroNexus functions to obtain more information about the data set and its groups.
Each function stores its result in the Seurat object, from where the export picks it up.

## Calculate percentage of mitochondrial and ribosomal transcripts

First, for every cell we calculate the percentage of mitochondrial and ribosomal transcripts of all transcripts using the `addPercentMtRibo()` function.

```{r addPercentMtRibo, eval=FALSE}
seurat <- addPercentMtRibo(
  seurat,
  organism = 'hg',
  gene_nomenclature = 'name'
)
```

## Get most expressed genes

Another interesting perspective is to look at the 100 most expressed genes for every group.
This can help in understanding the transcriptional activity of a given cell population.

```{r getMostExpressedGenes, eval=FALSE}
seurat <- getMostExpressedGenes(
  seurat,
  assay = 'RNA',
  groups = c('seurat_clusters','groups')
)
```

## Identify marker genes

Marker genes are genes which are particularly strongly or weakly expressed in a given cell population, e.g. a cluster.
This information can help to distinguish the role of different cell groups in the data set.
We can identify marker genes using the `getMarkerGenes()` function which internally uses the `Seurat::FindAllMarkers()` function but also stores the results in the Seurat object under the `misc` slot.

```{r getMarkerGenes, eval=FALSE}
seurat <- getMarkerGenes(
  seurat,
  assay = 'RNA',
  organism = 'hg',
  groups = c('seurat_clusters','groups'),
  name = 'cerebro_seurat',
  only_pos = TRUE
)
```

## Perform pathway enrichment on marker genes

Using the previously identified marker genes, we can perform a pathway enrichment analysis using the `getEnrichedPathways()` function.
The function will internally use the [Enrichr](https://maayanlab.cloud/Enrichr/) API and store the results in the Seurat object under the `misc` slot.
All we have to do is provide the name that we specified in `getMarkerGenes()`.

```{r getEnrichedPathways, eval=FALSE}
seurat <- getEnrichedPathways(
  seurat,
  marker_genes_input = 'cerebro_seurat',
  adj_p_cutoff = 0.01,
  max_terms = 100
)
```

## Gene set enrichment

On top of querying the databases of the [Enrichr](https://maayanlab.cloud/Enrichr/) service, one can also perform gene set enrichment analysis on gene sets provided as a `.gmt` file, e.g. from the [MSigDB](https://www.gsea-msigdb.org/gsea/msigdb/index.jsp).
The `performGeneSetEnrichmentAnalysis()` function uses the [GSVA](https://bioconductor.org/packages/release/bioc/html/GSVA.html) method in combination with additional statistics as published by [Diaz-Mejia et al.](https://f1000research.com/articles/8-296).

```{r performGeneSetEnrichmentAnalysis, eval=FALSE}
example_gene_set <- system.file("extdata/example_gene_set.gmt", package = "CerebroNexus")

seurat <- performGeneSetEnrichmentAnalysis(
  seurat,
  assay = 'RNA',
  GMT_file = example_gene_set,
  groups = c('seurat_clusters','groups')
)
```

# Optional extras

Two more kinds of information are exported if the Seurat object carries them.

## Cell cycle

If the meta data has a cell cycle column, e.g. `Phase` from Seurat's `CellCycleScoring()` (see the [Seurat cell cycle vignette](https://satijalab.org/seurat/articles/cell_cycle_vignette)), pass its name to the export with `cell_cycle = 'Phase'`.
The viewer then colours it with its cell cycle palette.
The example data has too few cell cycle genes to calculate it here.

## 3D projections

By default, every dimensional reduction except PCA is exported; one with three dimensions is shown as a 3D projection.

```{r umap_3d, eval=FALSE}
seurat <- RunUMAP(
  seurat,
  dims = 1:10,
  n.components = 3,
  reduction.name = 'UMAP_3D',
  reduction.key = 'UMAP3D_',
  verbose = FALSE
)
```

# Trajectories (optional)

A Monocle 2 trajectory can be attached to the Seurat object with `extractMonocleTrajectory()` before the export, and is then shown in the **Trajectory** tab.
See [Trajectory analysis](https://www.mheming.com/CerebroNexus/articles/trajectory_analysis.html) for the code.

# Export to Cerebro format

Finally, we use CerebroNexus `exportFromSeurat()` to export our Seurat object to a `.crb` file which can be loaded into CerebroNexus.

```{r export_data, eval=FALSE}
exportFromSeurat(
  seurat,
  assay = 'RNA',
  slot = 'data',
  file = paste0('cerebro_pbmc_seurat_', Sys.Date(), '.crb'),
  experiment_name = 'pbmc',
  organism = 'hg',
  groups = c('seurat_clusters','groups'),
  nUMI = 'nCount_RNA',
  nGene = 'nFeature_RNA',
  add_all_meta_data = TRUE,
  verbose = FALSE
)
```

By default the expression matrix is embedded in the `.crb`. For large data sets, add `expression_matrix_mode = "h5"` to write the matrix to a sibling `.h5` file instead (the only other storage mode); keep the two files together. A very large immune repertoire is moved to a third sibling file (`immune_sidecar = "auto"`). See [Store the expression matrix in H5 format](https://www.mheming.com/CerebroNexus/articles/create_expression_matrix_in_h5_format.html).


# Open the result

Open the file in the CerebroNexus user interface with `launchCerebro()`.
Tables can be downloaded in CSV or Excel format.

For a direct image export, click **Download PNG** in the plot toolbar. If the current view supports portable sharing, you can instead open **Share view** and click **Download PNG** there. The Share view dialog also lets you download or open a portable JSON configuration containing the current display state and selected cell barcodes, so the same view can be restored in another compatible CerebroNexus session without including the source data.

# See also

If your Seurat v5 assay is split into one layer per sample, see
[Seurat v5 layered assays: complete and safe expression matrices](https://www.mheming.com/CerebroNexus/articles/seurat_v5_layered_assays.html)
for the automatic resolution rules, custom-layer safeguards, and troubleshooting
steps.
